name: Ca' d'Zan

dates.note: Wikipedia: 'Cà d'Zan was built in the mid-1920s as the winter retreat of the American circus mogul ... John Ringling' and 'Completed in 1926 by Owen Burns'. The style node's exemplar carries 1926 and its note '1924-26'.

refs.title: Ca' d'Zan - Wikipedia
refs.note: The infobox gives 'Area 36,000 square feet (3,300 m2)', 'Architect Dwight James Baum', 'Architectural style Mediterranean revival'. The article: 'Cà d'Zan features an eclectic array of architectural styles including Venetian Gothic, Italian Renaissance, Moorish, and Spanish-inspired elements drawn from different historic periods.'

refs.title: Caples'-Ringlings' Estates Historic District, National Register ID 82001039, designated a contributing property 15 December 1982 — a DISTRICT listing covering several estates, of which this house is one; the house carries no individual National Register number in the source read

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026. No HABS survey was found and none is asserted. The 36,000 sq ft comes from the encyclopaedia infobox and is left in a ref note rather than carried as a `measurement`, which indexes survey quotes. NOTE for the one-building-one-record guard: the National Register number here is the Caples'-Ringlings' Estates Historic DISTRICT's, not this house's, and its title says so; it may legitimately be shared with any other contributing property that gets a record.
